chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ شَمُّونٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي الْمِقْدَامِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ع أَنَّهُ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam from his father from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

chunks.arabic_text: يَا أَبَا الْمِقْدَامِ إِنَّمَا شِيعَةُ عَلِيٍّ ص الشَّاحِبُونَ النَّاحِلُونَ الذَّابِلُونَ ذَابِلَةٌ شِفَاهُهُمْ مِنَ الْقِيَامِ خَمِيصَةٌ بُطُونُهُمْ مُصْفَرَّةٌ أَلْوَانُهُمْ مُتَغَيِّرَةٌ وُجُوهُهُمْ إِذَا جَنَّهُمُ اللَّيْلُ اتَّخَذُوا الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَاسْتَقْبَلُوهَا بِجِبَاهِهِمْ بَاكِيَةٌ عُيُونُهُمْ كَثِيرَةٌ دُمُوعُهُمْ صَلَاتُهُمْ كَثِيرَةٌ وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ كَثِيرٌ تِلَاوَتُهُمْ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ يَفْرَحُونَ يَفْرَحُ النَّاسُ وَهُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

translations.en: O Abu al-Miqdam, the Shia of Ali (peace be upon him) are only the pale, the thin, and the withered. Their lips are faded from standing (in prayer), their stomachs are atrophied, their complexions are changed, and their faces [are radiant]. When night covers them, they take the earth as a bed and face it with their foreheads. Their eyes are weeping, their tears are abundant, their prayers are plentiful, and their supplications are numerous. They recite the Book of Allah. When people are happy, they are grieved.

en.summary: In this famous hadith from *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) defines the 'Shi'a of Ali' not merely by political allegiance but by visible asceticism (*zuhd*) and spiritual exhaustion from worship, characterized by pale faces and yellowed bellies. This description highlights the dialectic of *farah* (joy in the Hereafter) and *huzn* (sorrow for worldly distractions), establishing a theological framework where true devotion manifests as a distinct emotional and physical state separate from societal norms. The narration underscores the concept of *al-Shi'a* as a spiritual vanguard whose identity is marked by endurance in prayer and deep contemplation of the Quran.
en.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of the true Shia of Imam Ali according to this hadith?

key_terms.الشَّاحِبُونَ: The pale-faced, indicating asceticism and lack of worldly indulgence
key_terms.النَّاحِلُونَ: The thin, indicating weight loss from fasting or worship
key_terms.الذَّابِلُونَ: The withered, showing the effects of prolonged standing in prayer
